title: Monoidal adjunctions lift to module objects
statement:
Let $F\colon\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D\colon G$ be a monoidal adjunction
$F\dashv G$. That is, $F$ is strong monoidal, $G$ is lax monoidal, and the lax structure
of $G$ is the mate of the monoidal structure of $F$. Let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object
of $\mathcal C$. The unit $u_{\mathcal R}\colon\mathcal R\to GF\mathcal R$ is a morphism of
monoid objects, for the structure on $GF\mathcal R$ transported along $F$ and then $G$
([def-sfb-modobj-transport]). There is an adjunction
$$
\operatorname{mapMod}(F)\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{u_{\mathcal R}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(G)
\colon\Mod_{F\mathcal R}(\mathcal D)\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C),
$$
with $\operatorname{Res}$ as in [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. On morphisms it is the
adjunction bijection of $F\dashv G$: an $F\mathcal R$-linear map $FM\to N$ corresponds to an
$\mathcal R$-linear map $M\to GN$, where $\mathcal R$ acts on $GN$ through $u_{\mathcal R}$.

proof.text:
Write $\mu^F,\mu^G$ for the tensor structure maps, $e^F,e^G$ for their unit maps, $\delta=(\mu^F)^{-1}$, and $u,c$ for the adjunction unit and counit. By [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit], both $u$ and $c$ are monoidal. Expanding the composite lax structures gives $u_{X\otimes Y}=G(\mu^F_{X,Y})\mu^G_{FX,FY}(u_X\otimes u_Y)$ and $u_{\mathbf1}=G(e^F)e^G$. Composing the tensor identity with $G\delta$ gives
$$G(\delta_{X,Y})u_{X\otimes Y}=\mu^G_{FX,FY}(u_X\otimes u_Y).$$
Likewise, monoidality of $c$ says $c_{A\otimes B}F(\mu^G_{A,B})\mu^F_{GA,GB}=c_A\otimes c_B$. Precomposing with $\delta_{GA,GB}$ gives
$$c_{A\otimes B}F(\mu^G_{A,B})=(c_A\otimes c_B)\delta_{GA,GB}.$$
These equations use invertibility only of the structure maps of $F$.

source.place: First paragraph, monoidality; second paragraph, tensor identity and its counit analogue

proof.text:
The twice-transported monoid structure is the one in [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Write $m$ and $a$ for the multiplication and unit of $\mathcal R$. Naturality and the monoidal equations of [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit] give
$$u_{\mathcal R}m=GF(m)u_{\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R}=GF(m)G(\mu^F_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R})\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,F\mathcal R}(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes u_{\mathcal R})=m_{GF\mathcal R}(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes u_{\mathcal R}),$$
$$u_{\mathcal R}a=GF(a)u_{\mathbf1}=GF(a)G(e^F)e^G=a_{GF\mathcal R}.$$
Thus $u_{\mathcal R}$ is a monoid morphism, and restriction along it is defined by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction].

source.place: First paragraph, components of the unit at monoid objects

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal R$-module $M$ and an $F\mathcal R$-module $N$, write $\gamma_M,\gamma_N$ for their actions. By [def-sfb-modobj-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], the restricted action on $GN$ is $\beta_N=G(\gamma_N)\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,N}(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes GN)$. By the linearity definition in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], an $F\mathcal R$-linear $\varphi:FM\to N$ satisfies $\varphi F(\gamma_M)=\gamma_N(F\mathcal R\otimes\varphi)\delta_{\mathcal R,M}$. Set $\psi=G(\varphi)u_M$. Naturality of $u$, the unit tensor equation obtained from [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit], and naturality of $\mu^G$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\psi\gamma_M&=G(\varphi F(\gamma_M))u_{\mathcal R\otimes M}\\
&=G(\gamma_N)G(F\mathcal R\otimes\varphi)G(\delta_{\mathcal R,M})u_{\mathcal R\otimes M}\\
&=G(\gamma_N)G(F\mathcal R\otimes\varphi)\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,FM}(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes u_M)\\
&=G(\gamma_N)\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,N}(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes G(\varphi)u_M)=\beta_N(\mathcal R\otimes\psi).
\end{aligned}$$
This is precisely $\mathcal R$-linearity of $\psi$.

Conversely, let $\psi:M\to GN$ be $\mathcal R$-linear for the action $\beta_N$ just specified by [def-sfb-modobj-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], and put $\varphi=c_NF(\psi)$. Then $\psi\gamma_M=G(\gamma_N)\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,N}(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes\psi)$. Apply $F$ and postcompose with $c_N$. Naturality of $c$ at $\gamma_N$, its tensor equation from [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit], naturality of $\delta$, and the triangle $c_{F\mathcal R}F(u_{\mathcal R})=\mathrm{id}_{F\mathcal R}$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varphi F(\gamma_M)&=c_NF(G(\gamma_N))F(\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,N})F(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes\psi)\\
&=\gamma_Nc_{F\mathcal R\otimes N}F(\mu^G_{F\mathcal R,N})F(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes\psi)\\
&=\gamma_N(c_{F\mathcal R}\otimes c_N)\delta_{GF\mathcal R,GN}F(u_{\mathcal R}\otimes\psi)\\
&=\gamma_N(c_{F\mathcal R}F(u_{\mathcal R})\otimes c_NF(\psi))\delta_{\mathcal R,M}\\
&=\gamma_N(F\mathcal R\otimes\varphi)\delta_{\mathcal R,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
Precomposing this equality with $\mu^F_{\mathcal R,M}$ turns this into $\varphi F(\gamma_M)\mu^F_{\mathcal R,M}=\gamma_N(F\mathcal R\otimes\varphi)$, the linearity condition of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] for the transported module $FM$.

source.place: Second paragraph, the omitted converse computation with the counit

proof.text: The maps $\varphi\mapsto G(\varphi)u_M$ and $\psi\mapsto c_NF(\psi)$ are inverse because they are the given underlying adjunction bijection and its inverse. Steps 3–4 show that they restrict to module morphisms. Module morphisms are the underlying morphisms satisfying the action equation, with underlying composition, by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For module maps $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$, naturality of the underlying adjunction therefore reads $\Phi(\varphi F(a))=\Phi(\varphi)a$ and $\Phi(b\varphi)=G(b)\Phi(\varphi)$ as identities of module morphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] these restricted natural bijections define the required adjunction between $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{u_{\mathcal R}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$; its hom bijection is exactly the one stated in the item.

source.place: Final sentence, naturality and construction of the adjunction

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; converse and monoid equations expanded in full
